newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fujitsu to sell chip assembly line to China firm.
newsitem.headline: Fujitsu to sell chip assembly line to China firm.

text.p: Fujitsu Ltd said on Monday it expects to sell one of its semiconductor assembly lines to Chinese chipmaker Hua Yue Microelectronics Co Ltd after July.

The assembly line in Fukushima prefecture, northern Japan, which can produce up to 10,000 125-mm wafers a month for use in home appliances and audio equipment, is expected to be sold for less than 10 billion yen, a Fujitsu spokeswoman said.
It will be moved to China and Fujitsu plans to build a new line in Fukushima, the spokeswoman said. She did not elaborate.

Hua Yue, based in Zhejiang province, specialises in designing and glazing integrated circuits into silicon wafers. It has supplied its products to Fujitsu under the Fujitsu brand since 1995, the spokeswoman said.
Hua Yue will supply Fujitsu with chips from the purchased assembly line, but the spokeswoman declined to comment on the volume.
